forecasts.reason: Moving 23 steps from 24 to 20 px saves about 0.005 s per step, about 0.11 s. E033's rate suggests a cost of about 0.1 pp, so 3 seeds can't resolve a loss of at most 0.15 pp. Seeds 0–2 will probably land near the bar.

Dropping 12 cheap 20 px steps saves about 0.17 s. Stretching the schedule and re-drawing the RNG probably costs about 0.1–0.15 pp, which is not resolvable against the hypothesis's 0.1 pp bar. It will probably fail the 0.753 gate.

No conv1 weight-gradient or 31×31 pool backward for about 35 steps saves about 0.15 s, and bandwidth-bound savings have come in at face value. E037's 60% cliff probably carries over to conv1 at about half size, about −0.2 pp.
About 12 more truncated 32 px steps save about 0.1 s. Interpolating E037's −0.38 pp linearly gives about −0.13 pp, a rate of about 0.8 s/pp, which is worse than the epoch dial.
3 forward-only 32 px batches cost about 0.04 s. The BN-stat mismatch after the final Lookahead copy is real but small. My prior is +0.05 ± 0.2 pp, so reaching +0.15 pp held-out is unlikely.
At 16 px the small maps under-use the tensor cores, so 35 steps save only about 0.12 s. The 1×1 final map is a new regime and probably costs about 0.2 pp.
About 0.07 s saved on trial 0 is only about 0.02 s on the 3-trial mean, below the hypothesis's 0.05 s bar. The math is identical, so accuracy should be bit-identical.

cruxes: Does any time-neutral accuracy booster exist? I064's BN recompute is the last cheap candidate. If none does, every further time cut needs accuracy bought with steps at about 1.5–2.5 s/pp, and the tip at about 0.7525 pooled is already at the bar.
Is the loss from cutting low-resolution steps (I060, I061) really under 0.1 pp per 0.1 s? If it is, the cheapest remaining trades are in the 20/24 px phases rather than in the freeze or the width.
Does the PCIe judge discount the bandwidth-bound savings (freeze, detach)? If it does, the relative value of the compute-bound resizing and epoch levers rises.
structured_output.world_model: W3 (cost lens), after E038. The tip is E036: 5.314 s and 0.7532 on seeds 0–2, about 0.7525 pooled on fresh seeds, so there is no margin. Time ≈ about 0.25 s fixed plus the sum over steps of the per-step cost (about 0.016/0.021/0.026/0.032 s at 20/24/28/32 px). Freezing group 1 saves about 27% of a step. Remaining cuts by size: early-resolution steps cost about 0.1 pp per 0.1 s, freeze-dose moves cost about 0.8 s/pp (bad), and prepare cleanup saves only about 0.02 s. No booster has yet shown a held-out gain. The likely best path: take the 40/0/30/30 split if accuracy holds, then stop trimming unless a booster appears.
